cards.title: THE LAUNDRY ROOM
cards.tagline: SIX ZONES. START AT THE MACHINES.
cards.objective: Laundry is the one job that arrives dirty, sits wet, and only counts as finished once it is back in a drawer. This card is the map and the order.
cards.start_here: LRZ-001 Washer and Dryer. Both machines first. Empty the drums, clear the lids, then pull the dryer out and look at what is behind it. Every other zone in this room is waiting on those two machines being ready to take a load.
how_to_play: 1. Deal the six ZONE cards face up. Pick the one that is annoying you today, or take the one this card says to start at.
2. Lay out that zone's three FRICTION cards. Keep the ones that are true in your laundry room. Put the rest back.
3. Turn a friction card over and pick the answer that is true. It names a ROOT CAUSE.
4. The root cause card names the ACTION cards that fix that cause. Pick the one that matches the time you actually have: fifteen or thirty minutes.
5. Do it standing up, with the card in your hand.
6. Read the victory condition out loud. If it is not true yet, you are not finished, and that is the whole scoring system.
7. Fill in the zone's STANDARD card with a pen and put it where the zone is.
8. Draw an EVENT card when an ordinary hard day happens, and see whether the standard held.
cards.players: 1 to 6. With more than one, deal the friction cards out and let each person keep the ones they believe. Disagreement is the useful part, not a problem to resolve before starting.
cards.six_s: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain
cards.safety_first: Do LRA-013 The Full Laundry Safety Walk before any rebuild. It takes thirty minutes and covers the duct, the hoses, the chemicals, the rack and every hung tool in the room.

cards.title: WASHER AND DRYER
cards.tagline: BOTH LIDS BARE. THE DUCT DATE ON THE TAPE.
cards.objective: Run loads reliably, and stay maintained well enough that the machines are never the reason laundry stops.
callouts: Washer door propped ajar, drum empty
Dryer drum empty behind its door
Bare surface across both lids
Lint screen back in its slot
A strip of masking tape on the dryer's side
Nothing stacked on either machine
cards.done_looks_like: Both drums empty with the washer door propped ajar, nothing at all sitting on either lid, a clean lint screen back in its slot, and a strip of masking tape on the side of the dryer with the month you last cleared the duct written on it.

safety_checks.question: Burn or fire
safety_checks.text: Lint packed in the duct behind the dryer, and lint on the heating element side of the screen housing. This is the highest heat and the most fuel in any indoor room outside the kitchen.

safety_checks.question: Water and electricity
safety_checks.text: Rubber fill hoses that have gone hard or bulged at the collar, sitting a hand's width from a wall outlet. A split hose sprays under pressure and does not stop until you reach the tap.

the_call.title: The duct you have not looked at
the_call.text: You have been telling yourself the dryer just runs a bit slow these days, and that towels have always needed two cycles. The dryer is not slow, it is blocked. The rule: if you cannot name the month you last pulled the machine out and cleared the duct, that is today's job, no debate. And while the dryer is already out and the duct is disconnected, look at what it is made of. If it is the flexible foil accordion kind, replace it with rigid metal now rather than promising yourself you will do it next time, because there is rarely a next time. Once a year is a cheap habit, and the failure it prevents burns the room it happens in.

cards.tagline: ONE OF EACH KIND. THE DOSE LINE INKED.
cards.objective: Hold the chemistry that actually gets used, at a dose you can measure and out of a child's reach.

cards.done_looks_like: One working detergent, one bleach, one tub of oxygen powder and one stain treatment standing on a wipeable tray, the pod tub latched and above shoulder height, the true dose line inked on the cap, and not one unlabeled bottle on the shelf.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Detergent pods within a child's reach, and bleach stored next to an ammonia based cleaner where a spill can mix the two into a gas in a small room with the door shut.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: A full jug of detergent stored above head height. Wet hands, a smooth handle, and a shelf you reach into blind is how a heavy bottle lands on a face.

the_call.title: The five half used stain removers
the_call.text: Every laundry shelf has them: a box of dye grabbing sheets, two spray bottles, a stick that dried solid in the cap, and something a relative swore by. You keep them because binning a mostly full bottle feels wasteful, so instead they sit there being wasteful slowly. The rule: keep the one treatment you have personally watched lift a stain, plus a tub of oxygen powder, which handles most of what the others promise. Everything else leaves today. A treatment you do not trust enough to reach for first is not a supply, it is a decision you have been postponing, and it is holding the one arm's reach of shelf next to the open washer lid.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush

the_call.title: The delicates bag that never fills
the_call.text: You sort into five streams because a care label once told you to, and one of those bags has been sitting a third full for three weeks while the thing you actually wanted washed waits inside it. The rule: a stream earns its own bag only if it has run as a full load, by itself, in the last month. Everything that fails that test merges into cold and gentle with a mesh bag inside the drum. Sorting is only worth doing when it produces a load you can run today, and a bag that waits three weeks is not sorting, it is a small pile of clothes you have taken out of circulation.

safety_checks.question: Burn or fire
safety_checks.text: An iron left face down or resting on its cord on the folding counter, with clean clothing stacked within reach of the soleplate.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: Baskets stacked high on the counter, and any wall cupboard above it loaded with heavy backstock over the spot where you stand and lean in to fold.

the_call.title: The single sock box
the_call.text: You are keeping a growing bag of unmatched socks because tomorrow the partner might surface. Occasionally one does, which is exactly why the bag never gets thrown out, and meanwhile it has become a permanent tenant on the one surface in this room that has to stay clear. The rule: singles get one shoebox and nothing larger. When the box is full, or at the change of season, whichever arrives first, everything still unmatched becomes a cleaning rag or leaves the house. A sock that has waited a whole season is not going to be reunited. It is just going to keep charging you the counter, and the counter is where the whole room jams.

safety_checks.question: Water and electricity
safety_checks.text: A drying rack standing over a wall outlet or across an extension lead, with garments dripping onto the floor beneath them.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: The wet patch under the rack on a hard laundry floor, walked over in socks by someone carrying a basket they cannot see past.

the_call.title: The garment that only ever hangs
the_call.text: There is at least one thing on that rack you have washed more times than you have worn. It is hand wash only, it takes two days to give up its water, and it holds the rack hostage the entire time while everything else waits its turn. The rule: think back to the last three times it was washed and name the occasion you wore it for each one. If you cannot name all three, the garment is charging you rack space and drying days it has not earned, and it goes. Line dry only is a real running cost, not a neutral care label, and it should only ever be paid for clothes you genuinely reach for.

cards.title: UTILITY AND CLEANING ZONE

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: Long handled tools leaned against a wall or stored behind a door, ready to swing down at head height when the door moves.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Drain cleaner and bleach kept at floor level next to the mop bucket, where they get knocked, decanted, or mixed during a rinse.

the_call.title: The rag pile
the_call.text: Worn towels, holed T-shirts and a retired set of sheets have quietly become a rag supply large enough to clean a small hotel. It grows because turning a worn item into a rag feels like thrift rather than a decision, so nothing is ever really discarded, only reclassified. The rule: rags live in one bin and only one bin, and nothing new becomes a rag until something old leaves as waste. If you cannot work through one bin of rags in a year, you are not saving cloth, you are storing it in the room with the least spare space. The same rule settles the second vacuum you are keeping for the garage: if it has not run in a year, it is not a spare, it is a broken machine with an excuse.

cards.title: EXCESS
cards.objective: More things are kept here than the zone's job needs.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Count what you used in the past month. If the honest number is a third of what is stored here, the space is not too small.

cards.objective: The thing has no single defined destination, so it lands wherever the hand opens.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask where one specific item lives. If two people answer differently, or nobody answers, it has no home.

cards.title: WRONG LOCATION
cards.objective: It is stored somewhere, just not where it is used.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Stand where you use it and count the steps to where it is kept. More than two is the wrong cabinet.
cards.instruction: This is a Straighten problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a folded stack of clean towels sitting on a laundry room shelf far from the bathroom cupboard they are meant to fill

cards.title: EXCESS MOTION
cards.objective: Getting it out means bending, lifting, unstacking, or moving something else first: too many steps.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Fetch it once and count the movements. More than two and the storage is charging you rent every time.

art.subject: a stepladder standing open in front of a laundry room wall cupboard, a single box of detergent visible on the shelf behind it

cards.title: POOR VISIBILITY
cards.objective: You own it, but you cannot see it, so you buy it again or forget it.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Open the door and, without moving anything, name what is at the back. If you cannot, that stock is invisible.
cards.instruction: This is a Straighten problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

cards.title: POOR ACCESSIBILITY
cards.objective: The people who use it cannot reach it safely, or at all.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Have the shortest person who uses this zone fetch what they need daily. If they climb, reach overhead, or ask for help, the height is wrong.
cards.instruction: This is a Safety problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a wall hook holding a broom mounted well above head height, a short step stool standing beneath it

cards.title: INSUFFICIENT CAPACITY
cards.objective: The right storage exists and genuinely cannot hold what belongs in it.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Put back only what belongs here. If it still will not close, or still stacks four deep, the capacity is the problem, not the habit.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a narrow laundry shelf with bottles and bins pressed edge to edge, one bin lid unable to close flat

cards.title: MISSING STANDARD
cards.objective: Nobody agreed what good looks like, so everybody is right.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask two people what this surface should look like at bedtime. Two answers means there is no standard to keep.

art.subject: a washing machine lid with a stray glove sitting on one half and bare surface on the other, no consistent state to either side

cards.title: MISSING TRIGGER
cards.objective: The reset is a good intention with nothing to attach it to.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Name the moment it happens. If the answer is "when I get round to it", there is no trigger and it will not survive a bad week.

art.subject: a dryer sitting finished and silent with a load of clothes still resting untouched inside its open drum

art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: SAFETY CONSTRAINT
cards.objective: The current arrangement can hurt somebody, and that outranks tidy.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Look for the four: a blade your hand would meet, weight above shoulder height, heat beside something that burns, and an unsafe placement near a child's reach.
cards.instruction: This is a Safety problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a bottle of drain cleaner sitting on a low shelf directly beside a stack of children's folded clothes
must_show: The current arrangement can hurt somebody, and that outranks tidy.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: CONFLICTING USERS
cards.objective: Two people run one zone by two designs, so it is permanently half of each.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Do the shared task together, once. The argument that starts is the conflict, and it is a design problem, not a character problem.
cards.instruction: This is a Standardize problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: two detergent scoops of different sizes sitting side by side on a laundry shelf, each showing a different dose line
must_show: Two people run one zone by two designs, so it is permanently half of each.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: UNCLEAR OWNERSHIP
cards.objective: Nobody specific is responsible for resetting this zone, so upkeep depends on whoever notices first.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask who resets this zone. If the honest answer is "whoever gets to it" or two names with no agreement, there is no owner.
cards.instruction: This is a Sustain problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a laundry basket of dry folded clothes sitting untouched on a counter with no note or name attached to it
must_show: Nobody specific is responsible for resetting this zone, so upkeep depends on whoever notices first.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: UNRESOLVED DECISION
cards.objective: The item is not clutter, it is a decision that has not been made, so it is stacked instead of acted on.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Pick up one piece. If your first thought is a verb (pay, sign, call, decide) rather than a place, it needs a decision, not a home.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a single unopened parcel sitting on an otherwise bare laundry folding counter, waiting
must_show: The item is not clutter, it is a decision that has not been made, so it is stacked instead of acted on.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: DIFFICULT TO CLEAN
cards.objective: Reaching the surface to clean it costs more effort than the rest of the zone combined, so it gets skipped.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Time how long it actually takes to reach and wipe the surface. If it requires moving something first, that cost is why it is skipped.

cards.title: PERCEPTUAL BLINDNESS
cards.objective: The clutter has been visible so long the eye stops flagging it as a problem.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask someone who does not live here to name what looks out of place. If they see it instantly and you had stopped noticing, this is the cause.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a stack of unmatched socks in a shoebox that has sat in the same corner of a laundry shelf long enough to gather a faint layer of dust

cards.title: EMPTY THE DRUMS AND DATE THE DUCT
cards.objective: Empty both drums, clear both lids, clear the lint screen, and write this month's date on the duct tape strip.
cards.why_it_matters: A drum you have to empty before you can fill is the single reason a household skips the last step of a wash day.
inputs: masking tape and a pen
the vent brush if the lint screen is due a clean
steps: Empty both drums, take everything off both lids, clear the lint screen and put it back, prop the washer door ajar, and write this month on a strip of tape on the side of the dryer.
Check the tape already on the dryer: if the month reads more than a year ago, treat the duct itself as this cycle's real job, not next month's.
Wipe down anything sticky left on either lid before you leave the room.
cards.victory_condition: Both drums empty, both lids bare, the door propped open, and a date on the dryer you can read from the doorway.

art.subject: a washer and dryer standing side by side with both doors open and their drums empty, a fresh strip of masking tape visible on the side of the dryer, both lids completely bare
must_show: Both drums empty, both lids bare, the door propped open, and a date on the dryer you can read from the doorway.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: PULL THE DRYER AND CLEAR THE DUCT
cards.objective: Disconnect the duct, clear what has built up behind the machine, and check the fill hoses while everything is already pulled out.
cards.why_it_matters: Lint packed behind the dryer is the highest fuel and the highest heat of any indoor room outside the kitchen, and a hose gone hard at the collar sprays without warning.
inputs: a step stool or helper to ease the machine forward
a vacuum with a hose attachment
rigid metal duct if the current run is a foil accordion
steps: Unplug the dryer and ease it forward on its feet far enough to reach the duct connection.
Disconnect the duct and vacuum out any soft grey packing built up at the bend behind the machine.
If the duct is a flexible foil accordion, replace the run with rigid metal now rather than promising to do it later.
Check both fill hoses for a hard or bulged collar while the machines are already pulled out, and replace either one that has gone stiff.
Push both machines back, level on their feet, and reconnect the duct fully before running the next load.
cards.victory_condition: The duct is clear and rigid where it can be, both fill hoses are supple at the collar, and both machines sit level on their feet.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a dryer pulled away from the wall with its duct disconnected, a small pile of grey lint cleared from the bend, a coil of rigid metal duct ready beside it
must_show: The duct is clear and rigid where it can be, both fill hoses are supple at the collar, and both machines sit level on their feet.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: ONE TRAY, ONE BOTTLE OF EACH
cards.objective: Bring every laundry product onto one tray, keep one working bottle of each kind, ink the true dose line, and latch the pod tub high.
cards.why_it_matters: A second open bottle of the same product almost always means the first one had gone invisible, and a low, unlatched pod tub is a poisoning risk in a house with children.
inputs: a permanent marker
a wipeable tray
a high shelf or latch for the pod tub
steps: Bring every laundry product onto one wipeable tray. Keep one working bottle of each kind, ink the true dose line on each cap, and latch the pod tub above shoulder height.
Recycle the empty or near-empty duplicate the moment the working bottle is confirmed.
Wipe the shelf under the tray before anything goes back onto it.
cards.victory_condition: One of each kind standing on a wipeable tray, a dose line you can see on every cap, and nothing a child can reach.

art.subject: a wipeable tray on a laundry shelf holding one bottle of each product with a marked dose line on each cap, an empty duplicate bottle set aside for recycling, a latched pod tub on a shelf above shoulder height
must_show: One of each kind standing on a wipeable tray, a dose line you can see on every cap, and nothing a child can reach.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: SEPARATE THE SHELF FROM THE FLOOR
cards.objective: Move bleach away from any ammonia-based cleaner, fix the shelf bracket if it is corroding, and give the tray a rinse.
cards.why_it_matters: Bleach and an ammonia-based cleaner sharing a shelf, or a bucket, can mix into a gas in a small room with the door shut.
inputs: a spare shelf or bracket if the bleach shelf is corroding
the drip tray
a permanent marker
steps: Move bleach and any ammonia-based cleaner onto separate shelves, never sharing a tray or a bucket.
Check the bracket under the bleach shelf for rust or corrosion from fumes, and replace it if it has started to give.
Carry the drip tray to the sink, scrub the tacky corners, dry it, and set it back under the containers.
Write the job on the tray edge under each bottle, wash, whites, stains, so a returned bottle lands in its own footprint.
cards.victory_condition: Bleach and any ammonia-based cleaner sit on separate shelves, the bracket underneath is sound, and the tray is clean and marked by job.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a laundry shelf with a bleach bottle standing well apart from an ammonia-based cleaner, a clean drip tray beneath them with each spot marked by its job
must_show: Bleach and any ammonia-based cleaner sit on separate shelves, the bracket underneath is sound, and the tray is clean and marked by job.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: CUT TO THREE BAGS
cards.objective: Cut the sorting streams to three, label those bags, stand them clear of the walking line, and add a dish for pockets.
cards.why_it_matters: A bag that stays a third full for weeks is not sorting, it is clothes taken out of circulation.
inputs: three bags
a marker or labels
a small dish
steps: Cut the sorting streams to the three this household will actually honour, label those three bags, stand them clear of the walking line, and put an empty dish on the shelf for pockets.
Empty any spare hamper you were holding for a stream that never filled on its own.
Check the floor in front of the washer door is bare before you leave.
cards.victory_condition: Three labelled bags, none above half full, bare floor in front of the washer door, and a dish holding only today's pocket contents.

art.subject: three labelled laundry sorting bags standing against a wall clear of an open floor path, a small dish on a shelf nearby, bare floor visible in front of a washing machine
must_show: Three labelled bags, none above half full, bare floor in front of the washer door, and a dish holding only today's pocket contents.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: MOVE THE BAGS OUT OF THE WALKING LINE
cards.objective: Reposition every sorting bag off the walking line and out of reach of a utility knife or blade riding home in a pocket.
cards.why_it_matters: A hamper in the walking line is a fall you take with your arms full, and reaching blind into a bag of work clothes is how a blade finds a hand.
inputs: hooks or a low shelf for the bags
a small parts tray for pocket finds
steps: Walk the path from the door to the machines and move any bag standing in that line to the side.
Fix a hook or shelf for each bag so it has a real spot away from the walking line.
Add a rule out loud: check every pocket by hand before it goes in the bag, not by reaching in blind later.
Confirm the dish on the shelf catches what pockets hold, so nothing sharp waits at the bottom of a bag.
cards.victory_condition: Every bag sits clear of the walking line at a reachable height, and pockets are checked going in, not pulled out blind.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: laundry sorting bags mounted on wall hooks well clear of a walking path between a door and washing machines
must_show: Every bag sits clear of the walking line at a reachable height, and pockets are checked going in, not pulled out blind.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: CLEAR THE COUNTER AND DELIVER THE BASKETS
cards.objective: Clear the counter completely, set one empty basket per bedroom underneath, hang six spare hangers, and deliver every clean item in the room.
cards.why_it_matters: Clean clothes with nowhere to go are the reason a dry load goes back in for a second tumble.
inputs: one basket per bedroom
six spare hangers
steps: Clear the counter completely, put one empty basket per bedroom underneath it, hang six spare hangers on the rail at the end, and take every piece of clean clothing in this room to the bedroom it belongs in.
Wipe the bare counter once it is cleared, before the next load lands on it.
Confirm no basket is left sitting full on the floor instead of stacked under the counter.
cards.victory_condition: A counter bare enough to roll pastry on, an empty basket per bedroom beneath it, and no clean clothing left in the room.

art.subject: a completely bare laundry folding counter with empty baskets stacked underneath it and six spare hangers on a rail at one end
must_show: A counter bare enough to roll pastry on, an empty basket per bedroom beneath it, and no clean clothing left in the room.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: NAME WHO DELIVERS THE BASKET
cards.objective: Split folding and delivery into two named jobs so the folder does not end up owning the whole chain.
cards.why_it_matters: One person folding and delivering for everybody is how the baskets quietly become where clean clothes live.
inputs: nothing beyond a short conversation with the household
steps: Name the folder for this load and the deliverer for each basket, out loud, even if they are the same person today.
Agree the delivery happens the same evening the basket is filled, not whenever there is time.
Photograph the bare counter and keep the photo somewhere visible, so 'clear' has one agreed picture rather than a guess.
Check the wardrobes the baskets deliver to are not already full; if they are, that capacity problem belongs to the bedroom, not this counter.
cards.victory_condition: A named folder and a named deliverer for every load, and no basket sits full past the same evening it was filled.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: an empty laundry folding counter with a small photograph taped inside a nearby cupboard door showing the counter in its bare state
must_show: A named folder and a named deliverer for every load, and no basket sits full past the same evening it was filled.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: STRIP THE RACK AND FOLD IT FLAT
cards.objective: Take off everything washed before today, put dry things away, empty the tray, and fold the rack flat.
cards.why_it_matters: A rack that never folds flat has become a second wardrobe, not a drying rack.
inputs: nothing beyond fifteen minutes and the rack itself
steps: Take everything off the rack that was washed before today, put the dry things away, wipe out the drip tray, fold the rack flat against the wall, and put six spare hangers on the rail.
Check the drip tray corners for standing water before you fold the rack away.
Confirm nothing at all is left hanging when you are done.
cards.victory_condition: The rack folded flat with dry bars, an empty tray beneath it, and nothing hanging that was not washed today.

art.subject: a drying rack folded completely flat against a wall with an empty drip tray resting beside it
must_show: The rack folded flat with dry bars, an empty tray beneath it, and nothing hanging that was not washed today.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: GIVE THE RACK ROOM TO BREATHE
cards.objective: Space items apart on the rack, add air movement if the room is damp, and move overflow to the wardrobes it belongs in.
cards.why_it_matters: Items hung overlapping never dry in the middle, and a room with no moving air turns the rack into a permanent fixture.
inputs: a small fan, if the room has no window or extractor
space in the household's wardrobes for what the rack is holding long-term
steps: Hang each item with a hand's width of space from the next, rather than pressed together.
If the room has no window or extractor, point a small fan along the rack rather than reaching for a bigger rack.
Sort what has been up longer than a week: if the wardrobe it belongs in is full, fix that capacity problem directly instead of leaving the item on the rack.
Wipe the wall and floor behind the rack where splash marks have built up.
cards.victory_condition: Every item on the rack has visible space around it, air is moving through the room, and nothing has been up longer than a week without a reason.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: garments hanging on a drying rack with a clear hand's width of space between each one, a small fan pointed along the length of the rack
must_show: Every item on the rack has visible space around it, air is moving through the room, and nothing has been up longer than a week without a reason.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: HANG THE TOOLS AND OUTLINE THEIR HOMES
cards.objective: Hang the broom, mop and dustpan heads up, mark an outline behind each, gather every attachment into one caddy, and empty the bucket into its taped square.
cards.why_it_matters: A tool that leans against a wall is a tool that will end up on the floor, and an outline is the only thing that reports a missing tool from the doorway.
inputs: a marker, paint pen, or tape for the outlines
a labelled caddy
tape for the bucket's floor square
steps: Hang the broom, mop and dustpan heads up and mark an outline behind each one, gather every vacuum attachment into one labelled caddy, and empty the bucket and stand it inside a taped square on the floor.
Knock any wound hair or lint off the dustpan and broom before you hang them.
Confirm the outlines are visible from the doorway, not hidden behind the door swing.
cards.victory_condition: Three handles off the floor with outlines showing behind them, every attachment in one caddy, and an empty bucket standing in its square.

art.subject: a broom, mop and dustpan hanging heads up on a wall with a painted outline behind each, a labelled caddy of vacuum attachments nearby, an empty bucket standing in a taped floor square
must_show: Three handles off the floor with outlines showing behind them, every attachment in one caddy, and an empty bucket standing in its square.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: SEPARATE THE CHEMICALS FROM THE BUCKET
cards.objective: Move drain cleaner and bleach up off the floor, away from the mop bucket, and confirm nothing leans behind the door.
cards.why_it_matters: Drain cleaner and bleach kept at floor level next to the mop bucket get knocked, decanted or mixed during a rinse, and anything leaned behind a door swings down at head height.
inputs: a shelf above the bucket for chemicals
wall hooks for anything currently leaning
steps: Move drain cleaner and bleach onto a shelf above the bucket, never inside or beside it.
Walk the room for anything leaning against a wall behind a door, and hang or bin it instead.
Check the shelf bracket under the chemicals for corrosion from fumes, and fix or replace it if it has started to give.
Wipe the bottle exteriors and the shelf, keeping the cloth off the labels so they stay readable.
cards.victory_condition: Drain cleaner and bleach sit on a shelf above the bucket, nothing leans behind the door, and the shelf bracket is sound.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a laundry chemical shelf holding drain cleaner and bleach well above an empty mop bucket standing on the floor beneath
must_show: Drain cleaner and bleach sit on a shelf above the bucket, nothing leans behind the door, and the shelf bracket is sound.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE FULL LAUNDRY SAFETY WALK
cards.objective: Walk the whole room once, standing where you use it, and confirm nothing hot, wet, heavy or overlooked could hurt somebody.
cards.why_it_matters: The things that hurt people in this room, a blocked duct, a hard fill hose, a chemical within reach, a tool that swings down, do not show up unless you look on purpose, and a room used every week stops getting looked at.
inputs: nothing beyond thirty minutes and a working set of hands
steps: Check the dryer duct and both fill hoses for the signs named in the Washer and Dryer zone: soft packing, a hard or bulged collar.
Check the pod tub and any chemical shelf are latched or out of a child's reach, and that bleach sits apart from anything ammonia based.
Check the drying rack and its drip tray are not standing in water on a hard floor.
Check nothing leans against a wall behind a door, and every long-handled tool is hung.
Fix anything you find right there, or write it down with today's date if it needs a part you do not have to hand.
cards.victory_condition: You can name, out loud, that the duct, the hoses, the chemicals, the rack and every leaning tool have each been checked today.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a wide view of a whole laundry room with a hand pointing in turn at a dryer duct, a chemical shelf and a wall-mounted broom, everything settled in its correct state
must_show: You can name, out loud, that the duct, the hoses, the chemicals, the rack and every leaning tool have each been checked today.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE FIVE MINUTE FETCH TEST
cards.objective: Fetch the item you use most in this room and count the movements it actually takes, then fix whichever one failed.
cards.why_it_matters: Extra steps to reach an everyday item are a cost paid every single time, and they hide in a room nobody times.
inputs: nothing beyond five minutes standing in the room
steps: Fetch the everyday detergent, the broom, and one clean hanger, counting the movements each one actually takes.
Anything past two movements, bending, unstacking, reaching overhead, moving something else first, gets a closer spot today.
Confirm the shortest person who uses this room could fetch the same three items without climbing or asking for help.
cards.victory_condition: The three everyday items each take two movements or fewer to fetch, and the shortest household member can reach all three unaided.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand reaching directly for a bottle of detergent on an easily reached shelf, no stool or extra items in the way
must_show: The three everyday items each take two movements or fewer to fetch, and the shortest household member can reach all three unaided.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: NAME WHO RUNS LAUNDRY DAY
cards.objective: Agree, out loud, who starts loads, who moves them, who folds and who delivers, so the room stops depending on whoever notices first.
cards.why_it_matters: Two people running one room by two designs is a permanent half-finished state, and a room with no named owner depends on whoever notices first.
inputs: nothing beyond a short conversation with the household
steps: Name, out loud, who starts a load, who moves it to the dryer or the rack, who folds, and who delivers each basket.
Agree on one dosing habit for the detergent cap, since two habits produce two different washes from the same jug.
Confirm the agreement against the room's own standard cards rather than leaving it as a conversation nobody can point back to.
Revisit the names the next time a load sits forgotten, rather than assuming the first agreement will hold forever.
cards.victory_condition: Every stage of a wash day has one named person, and both people who dose detergent use the same inked line.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a small chore board mounted on the wall beside the washing machine holding four tokens in a row, one for each stage of a wash day
must_show: Every stage of a wash day has one named person, and both people who dose detergent use the same inked line.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: WASHER AND DRYER STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Both drums empty, washer door ajar, lint screen cleared, before you leave the room.
cards.trigger: when the dryer buzzer sounds and you are still standing next to it
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Pull the dryer forward, check the duct for a soft grey buildup, and write this month on the tape strip if it is clear.
Lift the folds of the washer door gasket and wipe out whatever has collected in the seal.
Prop the washer door open a hand's width and check the lint screen is fully clear before you leave the room.

art.subject: a washer and dryer standing side by side, the washer door propped ajar with its drum empty, the dryer's door shut over an equally empty drum, both lids completely bare, a lint screen sitting clean in its slot on the dryer top, and a strip of masking tape stuck to the side of the dryer, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.objective: One product per job, standing on a tray, with the real dose line marked on the cap.
cards.trigger: when a jug runs empty and you are holding it
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Ink the true dose line on the cap of whatever bottle you use next, right at the machine.
Line up every bottle on the shelf and carry any second open jug of the same product to recycling.
Check the pod tub is latched and standing above shoulder height, and move it if it is not.

art.subject: a wipeable tray on a laundry shelf holding one bottle of detergent, one bottle of bleach, one tub of oxygen powder and one stain treatment standing side by side, a latched pod tub sitting on a higher shelf above shoulder height, and a dark ink line marked around the neck of the detergent cap, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines

cards.title: SORTING AND HAMPER ZONE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Every bag is a load, labeled by wash setting, and emptied before it passes half full.
cards.trigger: when you undress at the end of the day
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Tip the fullest sorting bag out and start that load right now, even if it is not the usual day.
Check the pocket dish on the shelf and empty anything sitting in it before the next load goes in.
Straighten each sorting bag so none of them stand in the walking line to the machines.

art.subject: three laundry sorting bags standing upright against a wall, each no more than half full and clear of the open floor path to a washing machine, a small dish sitting on a shelf nearby holding a single coin and a receipt, and a bare stretch of floor visible in front of the washer door, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines

cards.title: FOLDING SURFACE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: The counter is bare or holding one load, and every basket under it is empty before bed.
cards.trigger: when you tip a dry basket out onto the counter
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Carry one basket to its bedroom right now, even if the rest are not folded yet.
Clear anything off the counter that is not part of the load you are folding.
Hang one item that should not be folded onto the rail instead of stacking it.

art.subject: a laundry folding counter completely bare, a stack of empty baskets underneath it, six spare hangers hanging on a rail at one end, and no clean clothing anywhere else in the room, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines

cards.title: HANGING AND AIR-DRY ZONE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: The rack is in use or folded flat, never left standing half loaded.
cards.trigger: when you open the washer to start the next load
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Touch every item on the rack and carry off anything that is already dry.
Empty the drip tray and dry it before it goes back under the rack.
Fold the rack flat against the wall the moment the last item comes off it.

art.subject: a collapsible drying rack folded completely flat against a wall, its bars dry, an empty drip tray resting beneath it, six spare hangers on a rail beside it, and a clear stretch of floor where the rack usually stands open, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines

cards.title: UTILITY AND CLEANING ZONE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Nothing leans, nothing stores wet, and every hook has an outline behind it.
cards.trigger: when you clear the lint screen at the end of a wash day
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Hang the broom and dustpan back on their outlines instead of leaning them for later.
Rinse the mop head and hang it to dry before it goes back on the rail.
Check every vacuum attachment is in the caddy, and go find the one that is not.

art.subject: a broom, a mop and a dustpan hanging heads up on wall hooks with a painted outline visible behind each one, a caddy nearby holding every vacuum attachment in its place, the mop head hanging fully dry, and an empty bucket standing inside a taped square marked on the floor, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines

art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: LAUNDRY DAY WITH A SICK KID
cards.objective: A child is sick overnight, and every sheet, towel and set of pyjamas in the house needs washing before the next round starts.
cards.held_if: Both drums were already empty when the first load went in, and the sorting bags had room to take the sudden extra without spilling onto the floor.
cards.if_it_failed: If a load had to wait because the drum was already full, or the bags overflowed onto the floor, the machines or the sorting wall were not being kept at standard before this happened. Draw LRA-001 or LRA-005.
cards.instruction: Do not do anything to prepare. Live the day, then read the two lines below and be honest about which one you are.
cards.source: hand authored, not in the Manual

art.subject: a washing machine mid cycle with a full load of white bedding and pyjamas visible through the glass door, an empty laundry basket standing ready beside it
must_show: A child is sick overnight, and every sheet, towel and set of pyjamas in the house needs washing before the next round starts.
art.accept_test: The pressure has to be visible in the objects. No people, so the load has to be shown by what is on the surfaces.

cards.title: THE OVERNIGHT GUEST'S TOWELS
cards.objective: A guest stays the night and leaves behind two extra towels and a hand wash only sweater that needs to dry before they collect it.
cards.held_if: The extra towels found space on the counter without displacing anything already there, and the rack had room for one more hand wash item without crowding what was already hanging.
cards.if_it_failed: If the counter had to be cleared of other things first, or the rack was already full, the counter or the rack were not being kept clear as their own standard. Draw LRA-007 or LRA-009.
cards.instruction: Do not do anything to prepare. Live the day, then read the two lines below and be honest about which one you are.

cards.title: THE MUDDY SPORTS KIT
cards.objective: A sports kit comes home caked in mud and grass, tracking dirt across the laundry room floor on the way to the hamper.
cards.held_if: The kit went straight into its own bag without touching the floor for long, and the broom and dustpan were exactly where they belonged to clear the mess in under a minute.
cards.if_it_failed: If the mud sat on the floor while you hunted for the broom, the cleaning tools were not hanging in their outlines where this event needed them. Draw LRA-011.

cards.title: THE HOSE THAT LET GO
cards.objective: A fill hose splits without warning and sprays water across the floor before anyone reaches the shutoff valve.
cards.held_if: The hoses had been checked recently enough that this was a surprise rather than an overdue warning, and the mop and bucket were within reach to clear the water fast.
cards.if_it_failed: If the hose had already looked hard or bulged at the collar before it split, the machine's own safety check was overdue. Draw LRA-002. If the mop was not where it belonged, draw LRA-011.
cards.instruction: Do not do anything to prepare. Live the day, then read the two lines below and be honest about which one you are.

cards.title: THE WEEK WITH NO TIME TO FOLD
cards.objective: Three dry loads finish back to back during a busy week and nobody has ten minutes to fold any of them.
cards.held_if: The baskets from each load found a place under the counter without one being tipped onto the floor, and the sorting bags kept accepting new dirty clothes without backing up.
cards.if_it_failed: If clean laundry ended up in a pile on the floor because the baskets were already full, the one-basket-per-bedroom delivery habit had already slipped before this week started. Draw LRA-008.

cards.title: THE COLD SNAP WOOL SURGE
cards.objective: The temperature drops overnight and every wool jumper and hand wash item in the house needs washing and drying at once.
cards.held_if: A wool safe detergent was already on the shelf rather than needing an emergency trip to the shop, and the drying rack had room to take the sudden run of hand wash items.
cards.if_it_failed: If there was no wool safe detergent in the house, or the rack was already full of things that should have come down days ago, draw LRA-003 or LRA-009.
